source_text: In 2007, following the publication of three randomized controlled trials in South Africa, Kenya, and Uganda that demonstrated a 51–60% reduction in HIV acquisition risk among heterosexual men undergoing voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC), the World Health Organization (WHO) and Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) jointly recommended the scale-up of safe, voluntary VMMC services as part of a comprehensive HIV prevention package in 14 priority countries in eastern and southern Africa with generalized HIV epidemics and low prevalence of male circumcision.
